title: Oncall habit harvester and anonymized telemetry sampler
author: Morgan Lee
release_notes: Adds an opt-in on-call habit harvester and privacy-first telemetry sampler for incident-burst analysis. Default sampling is off; opt-in required. Includes new CLI, docs, and metrics.
description:
Motivation: on-call teams have asked for a low-friction way to collect anonymized, structured telemetry about common triage patterns (commands run, top signals inspected, mean time-to-first-action) so we can surface repeatable playbook candidates and quiet-window suggestions. This PR adds an opt-in "oncall-habit-harvester" to incident-bot that captures compact provenance + anonymized event histograms and ships them to a customer-configurable sink. Privacy is the priority: no raw logs, deterministic hashing of identifiers, histogram aggregation, and a configurable redaction pipeline.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a new CLI subcommand and background worker: incident-bot harvest start/stop/status. The worker aggregates events into per-shift buckets and emits periodic summaries.
- Implements a lightweight sampling layer that can operate in two modes: event-sampler (probabilistic) and behavior-aggregator (counts and top-k actions). Both modes support a customer-set sampling rate and an explicit allowlist for signal groups.
- Introduces an anonymization/redaction pipeline: stable salted hashes for user IDs, removal of known PII patterns, and token-level entropy checks to drop noisy, sensitive blobs.
- Adds telemetry metrics and traces: harvest.job.count, harvest.events.aggregated, harvest.redactions.skipped, harvest.ship.errors and tracing spans for harvest.lifecycle.
- Adds tests (unit + integration harness) and CLI docs with examples and upgrade notes.

Design decisions and privacy guards:
- Default is OFF. Customers must explicitly enable by setting harvest.enabled = true in incident-bot config or via CLI flag.
- No attachments or raw stack dumps are included in summaries; raw payloads are only used transiently inside the process and never persisted.
- Aggregation windows are coarse (default 4h) to avoid reconstructing individual sessions.
- Salt rotation: we support a rotation window; when rotated, older hashes are dropped from the aggregator to avoid long-lived linkability.

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/incident-bot/harvest.go - new CLI entry and runtime flags
- internal/harvest/worker.go - worker loop and aggregation logic
- internal/harvest/redact.go - redaction & hashing pipeline
- internal/harvest/sampler.go - sampling strategies and configuration
- docs/ops/harvest.md - admin-facing enablement and privacy FAQ
- test/integration/harvest_harness.go - ephemeral harness for end-to-end sampling tests
- pkg/metrics/harvest_metrics.go - new metrics exported to prometheus

Commits (summary):
- feat: add harvest CLI and worker scaffolding
- feat: implement probabilistic sampler and behavior aggregator
- feat: add redaction pipeline with black/allow lists and hashing
- test: integration harness for harvest pipeline and flakiness guards
- docs: admin enablement guide and privacy FAQ
- fix: retry logic for sink failures and graceful shutdown handling

Rollout and backward compatibility:
- no behavioral changes unless enabled. The new CLI is additive.
- Metrics use new names with a harvest.* prefix; dashboards should be added under the observability team guidance.
- If a customer enables the harvest sink but sink is misconfigured, worker will log a single incrementing error and back off; this prevents log storms and accidental data egress.

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests for redaction rules and sampler determinism.
- Integration harness that starts a local sink and validates the aggregated payloads meet size/PII constraints.
- CI initially showed lint failure (flake: formatting in harvest.go) and a unit test race in the integration harness. Fixes: formatting, and a mutex around the test harness registry. Final CI run: all checks passed.

Operational runbook notes:
- harvest.enabled defaults to false; on enablement, ops should verify harvest.ship.success metric within first hour.
- Alert: harvest.ship.errors > 5 over 10m triggers a temp disable for that instance and an automatic ticket to the ops channel (kept intentionally conservative).

Migration plan:
- Documentation provides a minimal checklist for customers: enable flag, set sink endpoint, choose sampling mode, run in audit mode for 24h to review sanitized summaries.

Related work: ENG-5123 (triage pattern discovery), PM-204 (quiet-hours product spec). This PR implements the backend scaffold required by the PM deck and provides a conservative privacy-first default.

Next steps: add a lightweight UI in the oncall console to visualize per-shift summaries and export candidate playbook snippets (follow-up PR).

review_conversation: Priya Patel: Nice end-to-end. Two privacy questions: 1) Why remove attachments instead of offering a configurable allowlist? 2) Can we make salt rotation explicit in the config and mention retention in the docs?

Morgan Lee: Good points. We intentionally exclude attachments by default to avoid accidental exfil. I've added an allowed-attachments list behind an "allow_attachments" admin flag and documented the risks. Salt rotation is configurable and documented; defaults to 90 days.

Ravi Singh: Code looks fine. Left a couple of nit comments about error messages in worker.go and a race on the test harness. Also: prefer smaller default aggregation window for dedicated deployments (opt-in override).
Morgan Lee: Addressed nit comments; added aggregation.window override and clarified behavior in comments. Fixed mutex on harness.
Dana Ortiz: CI flake fixed. Integration run passed locally. Approved pending a short changelog entry.
Priya Patel: Approved — privacy FAQ is clear and admin-facing examples look good.
